en: Vibhaṅga:
Analysis of the Heart of the Teaching (Dhammahadayavibhaṅga) 1.
The Section on the Compendium of All (Sabbasaṅgāhikavāra)

How many aggregates, how many bases, how many elements, how many truths, how many faculties, how many roots, how many nutriments, how many contacts, how many feelings, how many perceptions, how many volitions,
and how many consciousnesses? There are five aggregates, twelve bases, eighteen elements, four truths, twenty-two faculties, nine roots, four nutriments,
seven contacts, seven feelings, seven perceptions, seven volitions, and seven consciousnesses.
In this context, what are the five aggregates?
The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—
these are called "the five aggregates."
In this context, what are the twelve bases?
The eye base, the form base, the ear base, the sound base, the nose base, the odor base, the tongue base, the taste base, the body base, the tangible-object base, the mind base,
and the mental-phenomena base— these are called the "twelve bases."
In this context, what are the eighteen elements?
The eye element, the visible-form element, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element;
the nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the taste element, the tongue-consciousness element.
The body element, the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element, the mind element, the mental-phenomena element, and the mind-consciousness element—
these are called the "eighteen elements.
In this context, what are the four truths?
The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, the truth of cessation, and the truth of the path—
these are called the "four truths.
In this context, what are the twenty-two faculties?
The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the female faculty,
the male faculty, the life faculty, the pleasure faculty, the pain faculty, the joy faculty,
the grief faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, and the concentration faculty.
The faculty of wisdom, the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has already known—
these are called the twenty-two faculties.
In that regard, what are the nine roots?
There are three roots of the wholesome, three roots of the unwholesome, and three roots of the indeterminate.
In this regard, what are the three roots of the wholesome?
Non-greed is a root of the wholesome, non-hatred is a root of the wholesome, and non-delusion is a root of the wholesome.
These are the three wholesome roots.
In that regard, what are the three unwholesome roots?
Greed is an unwholesome root, hatred is an unwholesome root, and delusion is an unwholesome root.
These are the three unwholesome roots.
In that regard, what are the three indeterminate roots?
They are non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion, whether in relation to the results of wholesome states or in relation to states that are indeterminate as functional.
These are the three indeterminate causes.
These are called the "nine causes.
In that regard, what are the four nutriments?
Edible food, contact as nutriment, mental volition as nutriment, and consciousness as nutriment—
these are called the "four nutriments.
In this context, what are the seven types of contact?
Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-element-contact, and mind-consciousness-element-contact—
these are called the "seven contacts.
In this context, what are the seven feelings?
Feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact,
feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-element contact, and feeling born of mind-consciousness-element contact—
these are called the "seven feelings."
In this context, what are the seven types of perception?
Perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact,
perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-element-contact, and perception born of mind-consciousness-element-contact.
These are called the "seven perceptions.
In that regard, what are the seven volitions?
Volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact...
Volition, volition born of body-contact, volition born of mind-element-contact, and volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—
these are called the "seven kinds of volition.
In this context, what are the seven types of consciousness?
Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, mind-element, and mind-consciousness-element—these are called the "seven consciousnesses.
2. The Section on Arising and Non-arising.

2.1. The Sense-Sphere Realm (Kāmadhātu) In the sense-sphere realm, how many aggregates (khandha), how many bases (āyatana), how many elements (dhātu), how many truths (sacca), how many faculties (indriya), how many roots (hetu), how many nutriments (āhāra), how many contacts (phassa), how many feelings (vedanā), how many perceptions (saññā), how many volitions (cetanā), and how many consciousnesses (citta) are there?
In the sense-sphere realm, there are five aggregates, twelve bases, eighteen elements, three truths, and twenty-two faculties.
There are nine causes, four nutriments, seven contacts, seven feelings, seven perceptions, seven volitions, and seven consciousnesses.
In this context, what are the five aggregates of the sense-sphere realm?
They are the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.
These are called "the five aggregates of the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu).
In that regard, what are the twelve bases (āyatana) of the sense-sphere realm?

The eye base, the form base, the ear base, the sound base, the nose base, the odor base, the tongue base, the taste base, the body base, the tangible-object base, the mind base, and the mental-phenomena base.
These are called "the twelve bases of the sense-sphere of desire.
In that regard, what are the eighteen elements of the sense-sphere of desire? They are:
the eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element; [and so forth].
The nose element, the odor element, the nose-consciousness element; the tongue element, the flavor element, the tongue-consciousness element;

the body element, the tangible-object element, the body-consciousness element; the mind element, the mental-phenomena element, and the mind-consciousness element—these are called the eighteen elements of the sense-sphere (kāmadhātu).
In this context, what are the three truths of the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu)?
The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, and the truth of the path—
these are called "the three truths of the sense-sphere realm."
In this regard, what are the twenty-two faculties in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu)?
The eye faculty, the ear faculty … [and so on] … the faculty of one who has already known (aññātāvindriya)—
these are called "the twenty-two faculties in the sense-sphere realm."
In this context, what are the nine roots of the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*)?
They are the three wholesome roots, the three unwholesome roots, and the three indeterminate roots... [etc.
...These are called "the nine roots of the sense-sphere realm."
In this context, what are the four nutriments in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*)?
They are: physical nutriment, nutriment of contact, nutriment of mental volition, and nutriment of consciousness.
These are called "the four nutriments in the sense-sphere realm."
In this regard, what are the seven contacts of the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu)?
Eye-contact, ear-contact, nose-contact, tongue-contact, body-contact, mind-element-contact, and mind-consciousness-element-contact—
these are called "the seven contacts of the sense-sphere element."
In that regard, what are the seven feelings in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu)?
Feeling born of eye-contact, feeling born of ear-contact, feeling born of nose-contact, feeling born of tongue-contact,
feeling born of body-contact, feeling born of mind-element contact, and feeling born of mind-consciousness-element contact.
These are called "the seven feelings in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu).
In that regard, what are the seven perceptions in the sense-sphere realm?

Perception born of eye-contact, perception born of ear-contact, perception born of nose-contact, perception born of tongue-contact... [perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-contact].
Perception, perception born of body-contact, perception born of mind-element-contact, and perception born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—
these are called the "seven perceptions in the sense-sphere realm.
In this context, what are the seven volitions in the sense-sphere realm?
Volition born of eye-contact, volition born of ear-contact, volition born of nose-contact, volition born of tongue-contact,
volition born of body-contact, volition born of mind-element-contact, and volition born of mind-consciousness-element-contact—
these are called the "seven volitions of the sense-sphere realm."
In this context, what are the seven types of consciousness in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu)?
Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, nose-consciousness, tongue-consciousness, body-consciousness, the mind-element (manodhātu), and the mind-consciousness-element (manoviññāṇadhātu)—
these are called the seven types of consciousness in the sense-sphere realm.

2.2. The Form Realm (Rūpadhātu) In the form realm, how many aggregates (khandha), how many bases (āyatana), how many elements (dhātu), how many truths (sacca), how many faculties (indriya) … [and so on] … how many types of consciousness (citta) are there?
In the form realm, there are five aggregates, six bases, nine elements, three truths, and fourteen faculties.
Eight causes, three nutriments, four contacts, four feelings, four perceptions, four volitions, and four consciousnesses.
Therein, what are the five aggregates in the form element?
The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.
These are called "the five aggregates in the realm of form.
In that regard, what are the six sense bases in the realm of form?
They are: the eye base, the form base, the ear base, the sound base, the mind base, and the mental-object base.
These are called “the six bases in the form element.
In that regard, what are the nine elements in the form element? They are:

the eye element, the form element, the eye-consciousness element; the ear element, the sound element, the ear-consciousness element; the mind element, the mental-object element, and the mind-consciousness element.
These are called the nine elements within the form element (*rūpadhātu*).
In that regard, what are the three truths within the form element?
The truth of suffering (*dukkhasacca*), the truth of the origin (*samudayasacca*), and the truth of the path (*maggasacca*).
These are called "the three truths in the form element.
In that regard, what are the fourteen faculties in the form element?
They are: the eye faculty, the ear faculty, the mind faculty, the life faculty, the faculty of mental pleasure, and the faculty of equanimity.

The faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of "I shall come to know the unknown," the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has known—
these are called the fourteen faculties in the form element.
In that regard, what are the eight roots in the form element?
They are the three wholesome roots, the two unwholesome roots, and the three indeterminate roots.
In that regard, what are the three wholesome roots?
Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hatred is a wholesome root, and non-delusion is a wholesome root—
these are the three wholesome roots.
In this context, what are the two unwholesome roots?
Greed is an unwholesome root; delusion is an unwholesome root—these are the two unwholesome roots.
In this context, what are the three indeterminate roots?
Non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion— whether as the resultants of wholesome states or among the functionally indeterminate states—
these three are the indeterminate roots.
These are called the eight roots in the form element.
In that regard, what are the three nutriments in the form element?
The nutriment of contact, the nutriment of mental volition, and the nutriment of consciousness—
these are called "the three nutriments in the form element."
In this context, what are the four types of contact in the form element?
Eye-contact, ear-contact, mind-element-contact, and mind-consciousness-element-contact—
these are called "the four types of contact in the form element."
Therein, what are the four feelings in the form element?
… [and so on] … the four perceptions … [and so on] … the four volitions … [and so on].
What are the four types of consciousness?
Eye-consciousness, ear-consciousness, the mind-element, and the mind-consciousness-element—these are called "the four types of consciousness in the form element. –12
2.3. The Formless Element (Arūpadhātu) In the formless element, how many aggregates …pe… how many consciousnesses are there?

In the formless element, there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements, three truths, eleven faculties, eight roots, three nutriments, one contact, one feeling, one perception, one volition, and one consciousness.
In this context, what are the four aggregates in the formless element?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—
these are called "the four aggregates in the formless element."
In that regard, what are the two bases in the formless element?
The mind base and the mental-object base—
these are called the two bases in the formless element.
In that regard, what are the two elements in the formless realm?
The mind-consciousness element and the mental-object element—
these are called "the two elements in the formless realm."
In this regard, what are the three truths in the formless element?
The truth of suffering, the truth of the origin, and the truth of the path—
these are called "the three truths in the formless element."
In this context, what are the eleven faculties in the formless realm?

The mind faculty, the life faculty, the faculty of mental pleasure, the faculty of equanimity, the faculty of faith, the faculty of energy, the faculty of mindfulness, the faculty of concentration, the faculty of wisdom, the faculty of final knowledge, and the faculty of one who has attained final knowledge—
these are called the eleven faculties in the formless realm.
In this context, what are the eight roots in the immaterial element?
They are the three wholesome roots, the two unwholesome roots,
and the three indeterminate roots … [as above] … these are called “the eight roots in the immaterial element.”
In that regard, what are the three nutriments in the formless realm?
The nutriment of contact, the nutriment of mental volition, and the nutriment of consciousness—
these are called the three nutriments in the formless realm.
In that regard, what is the single contact in the formless element?
Contact associated with the mind-consciousness element—
this is called "the single contact in the formless element."
Therein, what is the one feeling in the formless element?
…pe… the one perception …pe… the one volition …pe…
One consciousness:
the mind-consciousness element—this is called "one consciousness in the immaterial element. –12
2.4. The Not-Included (Apariyāpanna) In the not-included [realms], how many aggregates are there? ...pe... How many consciousnesses are there?

In the not-included [realms], there are four aggregates, two bases, two elements, two truths, twelve faculties, six roots, three nutriments, one contact, one feeling, one perception, one volition, and one consciousness.
Therein, what are the four aggregates that are not included [within the mundane]?
The aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—
these are called "the four aggregates that are not included."
In this context, what are the two bases that are not included [in the mundane]?
The mind base and the mental-object base—
these are called "the two bases that are not included."
In this context, what are the two elements that are not included [in the mundane]?
The mind-consciousness element and the mental-object element—
these are called "the two elements that are not included."
In this context, what are the two truths that are not included [in the realms]?
The truth of the path and the truth of cessation—
these are called "the two truths that are not included."
In that regard, what are the twelve faculties not included [in the mundane]?

They are: the mind faculty, the life faculty, the pleasure faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, the wisdom faculty, the "I-shall-come-to-know-the-unknown" faculty, the final-knowledge faculty, and the final-knower faculty.
These are called the "twelve faculties in the unincluded.
Therein, what are the six roots in the unincluded?
They are the three wholesome roots and the three indeterminate roots.
In this regard, what are the three wholesome roots?
Non-greed is a wholesome root, non-hatred is a wholesome root, and non-delusion is a wholesome root—
these are the three wholesome roots.
In this context, what are the three indeterminate roots?
Non-greed, non-hatred, and non-delusion as the result of wholesome states—
these are the three indeterminate roots.
These are called the "six roots not included [within the mundane].
Therein, what are the three nutriments not included [within the mundane]?
They are: contact as nutriment, mental volition as nutriment, and consciousness as nutriment.
These are called "the three nutriments in the unincluded realm.
In that context, what is the one contact in the unincluded realm?
It is the contact associated with the mind-consciousness element.
This is called "a single contact in the unincluded [sphere].
Therein, what is "a single feeling in the unincluded" …pe… "a single perception in the unincluded" …pe…?
Is it one volition? ... [and so on] ...
Is it one consciousness?
It is the mind-consciousness element.
This is called "one consciousness in the unperturbed.
— 12. 3. The Section on the Perturbed and the Unperturbed. 3.1.
The Realm of Sensual Desire (Kāmadhātu).
Of the five aggregates, how many are included in the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu), and how many are not included in the sense-sphere element?
…pe… Of the seven types of consciousness, how many are included in the sense-sphere element, and how many are not included in the sense-sphere element?
The aggregate of form is included in the sense-sphere element.
The four aggregates may be included in the sense-sphere element (*kāmadhātu*), or they may not be included in the sense-sphere element.
Ten bases are included in the sense-sphere element;
two bases may be included in the sense-sphere element, or they may not be included in the sense-sphere element.
Sixteen elements are included within the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu);
two elements may be either included within the sense-sphere element or not included within the sense-sphere element.
The truth of the origin (samudayasacca) is included within the sense-sphere element.
Two truths are not included within the sense-sphere element (*kāmadhātu*);
the truth of suffering may be included within the sense-sphere element, and it may not be included within the sense-sphere element.
Ten faculties are included within the sense-sphere element.
Three faculties are not included in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*);
nine faculties may be either included in the sense-sphere realm or not included in the sense-sphere realm.
Three unwholesome roots are included in the sense-sphere realm.
The six causes may be included within the sense-sphere element (*kāmadhātu*), or they may not be included within the sense-sphere element.
Edible food is included within the sense-sphere element;
the other three nutriments may be included within the sense-sphere element, or they may not be included within the sense-sphere element.
Six contacts are included within the sense-sphere element (*kāmadhātu*);
the contact of the mind-consciousness element may be included within the sense-sphere element, or it may not be included within the sense-sphere element.
Six feelings... [and so on].
Six perceptions ... [and so on] ...
six volitions ... [and so on] ...
six types of consciousness are included within the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu).
The mind-consciousness element may be included within the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), or it may not be included within the sense-sphere realm.
3.2. The Form Realm: Of the five aggregates (*khandha*), how many are included within the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), and how many are not included within the form realm? …pe…
Of the seven types of consciousness, how many are included in the form element, and how many are not included in the form element?
The aggregate of form is not included in the form element;
the four aggregates may be included in the form element, or they may not be included in the form element.
Ten bases are not included in the form element;
two bases may be included in the form element, and may not be included in the form element.
Sixteen elements are not included in the form element.
Two elements may be included in the form element, or they may not be included in the form element.
Three truths are not included in the form element;
the truth of suffering may be included in the form element, or it may not be included in the form element.
Thirteen faculties are not included in the form realm;
nine faculties may be included in the form realm, and may be not included in the form realm.
Three unwholesome roots are not included in the form realm.
The six causes may be included in the form element, or they may not be included in the form element.
Edible food is not included in the form element;
the other three foods may be included in the form element, or they may not be included in the form element.
Six contacts are not included in the form element;
the contact of the mind-consciousness element may be included in the form element, or it may not be included in the form element.
Six feelings ... [and so on] ...
The six perceptions … the six volitions … the six consciousnesses are not included within the form realm.
The mind-consciousness element may be included in the form realm, or it may not be included in the form realm.
3.3. The Formless Realm:
Of the five aggregates, how many are included in the formless realm, and how many are not included in the formless realm? …pe…
Of the seven types of consciousness, how many are included in the formless realm (*arūpadhātu*), and how many are not included in the formless realm?
The aggregate of form (*rūpakkhandha*) is not included in the formless realm;
the four aggregates may be included in the formless realm, or they may not be included in the formless realm.
Ten bases are not included in the formless element;
two bases may be included in the formless element, and may not be included in the formless element.
Sixteen elements are not included in the formless element.
Two elements may be included in the formless realm, or they may not be included in the formless realm.
Three truths are not included in the formless realm.
The truth of suffering may be included in the formless realm, or it may not be included in the formless realm.
Fourteen faculties are not included in the formless realm;
eight faculties may be included in the formless realm, and may not be included in the formless realm.
Three unwholesome roots are not included in the formless realm.
The six causes may be included in the formless realm, or they may not be included in the formless realm.
Edible food is not included in the formless realm;
the other three foods may be included in the formless realm, or they may not be included in the formless realm.
Six contacts are not included in the formless element;
the contact of the mind-consciousness element may be included in the formless element, or it may not be included in the formless element.
Six feelings … [and so on] …
The six perceptions … the six volitions … the six consciousnesses are not included within the formless realm.
The mind-consciousness element may be included in the immaterial realm, or it may not be included in the immaterial realm.
3.4. Included and Unincluded:
Of the five aggregates, how many are included, and how many are unincluded? …pe…
Of the seven types of consciousness, how many are included (pariyāpanna) and how many are not included (apariyāpanna)?
The aggregate of form is included;
the four aggregates may be either included or not included.
Eight bases are included;
two bases may be either included or not included.
Sixteen elements are included.
Two elements may be included [within the mundane], or they may be unincluded.
Two truths are included;
two truths are unincluded.
Nine faculties are included [within the mundane]; three faculties are not included;
nine faculties may be either included or not included.
Three unwholesome roots are included.
The six causes may be included [within the mundane] or may be unincluded [transcendent].
Edible food is included;
the other three foods may be included or may be unincluded.
Six contacts are included [within the mundane];
the contact associated with the mind-consciousness element may be either included or not included.
Six feelings ... [and so on] ...
Six perceptions … [and so on] … six volitions … [and so on] … six consciousnesses are included within the mundane.
The mind-consciousness element may be included (pariyāpanna) or may be not included (apariyāpanna).
4. Section on the Vision of Phenomena (Dhammadassanavāra). 4.1.
The Sense-Sphere Element (Kāmadhātu).
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), how many aggregates (khandhā) manifest? ...pe... how many consciousnesses (cittāni) manifest?
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for all [beings], five aggregates manifest;
for some, eleven bases (āyatanāni) manifest.
For some, ten bases become manifest;
for some, another ten bases become manifest;
for some, nine bases become manifest.
For some, the seven sense bases manifest;
for some, eleven elements manifest;
for some, ten elements manifest.
For some, ten other elements manifest;
for some, nine elements manifest;
for some, seven elements manifest.
For all [noble ones], one truth becomes manifest;
for some, fourteen faculties become manifest;
for some, thirteen faculties become manifest.
For some, thirteen other faculties become manifest;
for some, twelve faculties become manifest;
for some, ten faculties become manifest.
For some, nine faculties become manifest;
for others, another set of nine faculties becomes manifest;
for some, eight faculties become manifest.
For some, eight other faculties become manifest;
for some, seven faculties become manifest;
for some, five faculties become manifest.
In some, four faculties become manifest;
in some, three roots become manifest;
in some, two roots become manifest.
In some cases they arise without a cause;
in all cases the four nutriments arise;
in all cases a single contact arises.
For all [beings], there is one feeling … pe … one perception … pe … one volition … pe …
A single consciousness manifests.

At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), which five aggregates manifest for all beings? The aggregate of form …pe… [the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and] the aggregate of consciousness.
The consciousness aggregate—
at the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these five aggregates manifest for all beings.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do eleven bases (*āyatana*) manifest?
For the gods of the sense-sphere, for humans of the first eon, for spontaneously born ghosts,
for spontaneously born asuras, for spontaneously born animals, and for those in hell who possess complete sense bases,
at the moment of rebirth, eleven sense bases become manifest.

The eye base, the visible-form base, the ear base, the nose base, the odor base, the tongue base, the taste base, the body base, the tangible-object base, the mind base, and the mental-phenomena base.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these eleven bases manifest for whom.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do ten bases manifest?
For spontaneously born ghosts (petas), spontaneously born asuras, spontaneously born animals, and those in hell—at the moment of birth, ten bases (āyatana) appear:

the base of visible forms, the base of sounds, the base of odors, the base of tastes, the base of tangibles, the base of the mind, and the base of mental phenomena; as well as the base of the eye, the base of the ear, the base of the nose, and the base of the tongue.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these ten bases appear for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), for whom do the other ten bases (āyatana) become manifest?

For spontaneously born (opapātika) ghosts (petas), for spontaneously born asuras, for spontaneously born animals (tiracchānagata), and for denizens of hell (nerayika); and for those who are congenitally deaf—at the moment of their rebirth, these ten bases become manifest:
the eye base, the visible-form base, the nose base, the odor base, the tongue base, the taste base, the body base, the tangible-object base, the mind base, and the mental-phenomena base.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these ten bases (*āyatana*) become manifest for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do nine bases become manifest?

For spontaneously born (*opapātika*) ghosts (*peta*), for spontaneously born asuras, for spontaneously born animals (*tiracchānagata*), for denizens of hell (*nerayika*), and for those who are blind from birth or deaf from birth—at the moment of their rebirth, nine bases become manifest.
The base of visible forms, the base of odors, the base of tastes, the base of tangible objects, the mind base, and the base of mental phenomena.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these nine bases manifest for beings.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do seven bases manifest?
At the moment of rebirth for beings born from a womb, seven bases appear:
the visible-form base, the odor base, the flavor base, the body base, the tangible-base, the mind base, and the mental-object base.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere element (kāmadhātu), these seven bases appear for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), for whom do eleven elements become manifest?
For gods of the sense-sphere realm; for humans who are first-born at the beginning of an eon; for spontaneously born (opapātika) ghosts (peta);
for spontaneously born asuras; and for spontaneously born animals and hell-beings whose sense bases are complete—at the moment of their rebirth.
Eleven elements become manifest:

the eye element, the visible-form element, the ear element, the nose element, the odor element, the tongue element, the taste element, the body element, the tangible-object element, the mind-consciousness element, and the mental-object element.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these eleven elements become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), for whom are ten elements (dhātu) manifest?

For spontaneously born (opapātika) ghosts (petā), for spontaneously born asuras, for spontaneously born animals (tiracchānagata), and for denizens of hell (nerayika)—and for those born blind—at the moment of rebirth, ten elements are manifest:

the element of visible form, the element of the ear, the element of the nose, the element of odors, the element of the tongue, the element of tastes, the element of the body, the element of tangibles, the element of mind-consciousness, and the element of mental phenomena (dhammadhātu).
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these ten elements (*dhātu*) become manifest for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do another ten elements become manifest?

For spontaneously born (*opapātika*) ghosts (*petā*), for spontaneously born asuras, for spontaneously born animals (*tiracchānagata*), for denizens of hell (*nerayika*), and for those who are congenitally deaf—at the moment of their rebirth, ten elements become manifest.

The eye-element, the form-element, the nose-element, the odor-element, the tongue-element, the taste-element, the body-element, the tangible-object-element, the mind-consciousness-element, and the mental-object-element.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these ten elements become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do nine elements become manifest?

For spontaneously born ghosts (petas), spontaneously born asuras, spontaneously born animals, and those in hell; for those who are blind from birth and deaf—at the moment of rebirth, nine elements manifest:

the visible-form element, the nose element, the odor element, the tongue element, the taste element, the body element, the tangible-object element, the mind-consciousness element, and the mental-object element.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these nine elements manifest for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), for whom do seven elements become manifest?
At the moment of rebirth for beings born from a womb, seven elements become manifest:
the visible-form element, the odor element, the taste element, the body-element, the tangible-object element, the mind-consciousness element, and the mental-object element.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these seven elements become manifest for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, which single truth becomes manifest for all?
The truth of suffering (dukkhasacca).
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), this one truth manifests for all beings.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do fourteen faculties (*indriya*) manifest?
For the gods of the sense-sphere realm who possess roots of merit and are associated with knowledge, fourteen faculties manifest at the moment of rebirth.
The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty,
the female faculty or the male faculty, the life faculty, the joy faculty or the equanimity faculty,
the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, and the wisdom faculty.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these fourteen faculties (*indriya*) become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do thirteen faculties become manifest?
For those gods of the sense-sphere realm who possess roots of merit (*sahetuka*) but are dissociated from knowledge (*ñāṇavippayutta*), at the moment of rebirth, thirteen faculties become manifest.
The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty,
the female faculty or the male faculty, the life faculty, the joy faculty or the equanimity faculty,
the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, and the concentration faculty.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these thirteen faculties (*indriya*) become manifest for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do another thirteen faculties become manifest?

For the humans who were the first beings of the eon (*paṭhamakappika*), who are possessed of roots of merit (*sahetuka*) and associated with knowledge (*ñāṇasampayutta*), at the moment of rebirth, thirteen faculties become manifest.
The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the life faculty,
the faculty of mental pleasure or the faculty of equanimity, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty,
the concentration faculty, and the wisdom faculty.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these thirteen faculties (*indriya*) become manifest for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do twelve faculties become manifest?

For humans who are first-born at the beginning of an eon (*paṭhamakappika*), who possess roots of merit (*sahetuka*), and who are dissociated from knowledge (*ñāṇavippayutta*), twelve faculties become manifest at the moment of rebirth.
The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the life faculty,
the faculty of mental pleasure or the faculty of equanimity, the faith faculty, the energy faculty,
the mindfulness faculty, and the concentration faculty.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these twelve faculties (*indriya*) become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do ten faculties become manifest?
For womb-born beings who possess roots of merit and are associated with knowledge, ten faculties become manifest at the moment of rebirth.
The body faculty, the mind faculty, the femininity faculty or the masculinity faculty, the life faculty, the joy faculty or the equanimity faculty,
the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, and the wisdom faculty.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these ten faculties become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), for whom do nine faculties become manifest?
For beings born from a womb who are possessed of roots but dissociated from knowledge, at the moment of rebirth, nine faculties become manifest:

the body faculty, the mind faculty, either the femininity faculty or the masculinity faculty, the life faculty, either the joy faculty or the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, and the concentration faculty.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these nine faculties (*indriya*) become manifest for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do another nine faculties become manifest?

For spontaneously born (*opapātika*) ghosts (*peta*), for spontaneously born asuras, for spontaneously born animals (*tiracchānagata*), and for denizens of hell (*nerayika*) with complete sense bases—at the moment of their rebirth, nine faculties become manifest.

The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the nose faculty, the tongue faculty, the body faculty, the mind faculty, the femininity faculty or the masculinity faculty, the life faculty, and the equanimity faculty—

At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), for whom do the other eight faculties become manifest?

For spontaneously born (opapātika) ghosts (petas), for spontaneously born asuras, for spontaneously born animals (tiracchānagata), and for denizens of hell (nerayika); and for those who are congenitally deaf—at the moment of rebirth, eight faculties become manifest:
the eye-faculty, the nose-faculty, the tongue-faculty, the body-faculty, the mind-faculty, either the female-faculty or the male-faculty, the life-faculty, and the equanimity-faculty.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these eight faculties become manifest for them.

At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these seven faculties manifest for those beings.

In womb-born beings who are without roots, with the exception of those who are neuter, five faculties become manifest at the moment of rebirth:

For beings born from a womb who are root-cause-free (ahetuka) and for those who are neuter (napuṃsaka), at the moment of rebirth, four faculties become manifest:
the body faculty (kāyindriya), the mind faculty (manindriya), the life faculty (jīvitindriya), and the equanimity faculty (upekkhindriya).
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these four faculties become manifest for them.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do the three roots (hetu) become manifest?

Non-greed is a resultant cause, non-hatred is a resultant cause, and non-delusion is a resultant cause.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), these three causes manifest for such [beings].
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, for whom do two causes manifest?
In the case of gods of the sense-sphere realm, humans of the first eon, and womb-born beings who possess roots but are dissociated from knowledge, at the moment of rebirth two roots become manifest:
non-greed as a resultant root and non-hatred as a resultant root.
In the sense-sphere realm, at the moment of rebirth, these two roots become manifest for them.
In the remaining beings, [the nutriments] arise without roots.

physical nutriment (kabaḷīkāra-āhāra), contact as nutriment (phassa-āhāra), mental volition as nutriment (manosañcetanā-āhāra), and consciousness as nutriment (viññāṇa-āhāra).
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (kāmadhātu), these four nutriments (āhāra) manifest for all beings.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, which single type of contact (phassa) manifests for all beings?
It is the contact associated with the mind-consciousness element (manoviññāṇadhātu).
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm (*kāmadhātu*), this single contact (*phassa*) manifests for all.
At the moment of rebirth in the sense-sphere realm, what is the single feeling (*vedanā*) for all? ... [and so on] ... what is the single perception (*saññā*) for all? ... [and so on] ...
Is there one volition …pe… does one consciousness manifest?
It is the mind-consciousness element.

The aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, these five aggregates manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, which five bases manifest?
The eye base, the visible-form base, the ear base, the mind base, and the mental-object base.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, these five bases become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, which five elements become manifest?
The eye element, the visible-form element, the ear element, the mind-consciousness element, and the mental-object element.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, these five elements become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, which one truth becomes manifest?
The truth of suffering.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), this one truth manifests.

The eye faculty, the ear faculty, the mind faculty, the life faculty, either the joy faculty or the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, and the wisdom faculty.

Non-greed as a resultant root, non-hatred as a resultant root, and non-delusion as a resultant root.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, these three causes become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, which three nutriments become manifest?
The nutriment of contact, the nutriment of mental volition, and the nutriment of consciousness.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, these three nutriments become manifest.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, which single type of contact becomes manifest?
Contact associated with the mind-consciousness element.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, this one type of contact manifests.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm, what is the one type of feeling? ... [and so on] ...
the one type of perception? ... [and so on] ...
Is there one volition …pe… does one consciousness manifest?
It is the mind-consciousness element.
At the moment of rebirth in the form realm (*rūpadhātu*), this one consciousness manifests. 4.3.

The sense-sphere of visible forms and the sense-sphere of mental objects;

The mind base and the mental-object base.

The mind-consciousness element (manoviññāṇadhātu) and the mental-object element (dhammadhātu).

The truth of suffering.

The mind faculty, the life faculty, the equanimity faculty, the faith faculty, the energy faculty, the mindfulness faculty, the concentration faculty, and the wisdom faculty.

Contact associated with the mind-consciousness element.

5. Section on the Demonstration of Different Planes of Existence:

States belonging to the sense sphere; states not belonging to the sense sphere; states belonging to the fine-material sphere; states not belonging to the fine-material sphere; states belonging to the immaterial sphere; states not belonging to the immaterial sphere; states that are included within the mundane; states that are not included within the mundane.
Which phenomena belong to the sense sphere (*kāmāvacara*)?
Taking the Avīci hell as the lower limit and including the Paranimmitavasavatti devas above, those aggregates, elements, and bases that have their range and inclusion within this interval—
namely, form, feeling, perception, mental formations, and consciousness.
These phenomena belong to the sense sphere.
Which phenomena do not belong to the sense sphere?
Those belonging to the fine-material sphere, those belonging to the immaterial sphere, and those that are unincluded.
These states do not belong to the sense sphere (*kāmāvacara*).
Which states belong to the fine-material sphere (*rūpāvacara*)?
Taking the Brahma-world as the lower limit and including the Akaniṭṭha devas at the upper limit, whatever...

In this interval, those states belonging to this sphere, included within this sphere— the mental and mental concomitant phenomena of one who has attained [jhāna], or one who has been reborn there, or one dwelling in happiness in this very life—
these phenomena belong to the fine-material sphere (rūpāvacara).
Which phenomena are not of the fine-material sphere?
Those of the sense-sphere, those of the immaterial sphere, and those that are unincluded—
these phenomena are not of the fine-material sphere.
Which phenomena belong to the formless realm (*arūpāvacara*)?

Taking as their lower limit the gods who have reached the sphere of infinite space (*ākāsānañcāyatana*), and taking as their upper limit the gods who have reached the sphere of neither-perception-nor-non-perception (*nevasaññānāsaññāyatana*),

whatever exists within this interval— whether it belongs there, is included therein, or pertains to one who has attained [a formless meditative absorption]— these are the phenomena belonging to the formless realm.
The states of mind and mental factors of one who has been reborn [in the formless realm] or of one dwelling in happiness in this very life—
these states are form-sphere (arūpāvacara).
Which states are not form-sphere?
Those pertaining to the sense sphere, those pertaining to the fine-material sphere,
and those that are non-included— these states are not pertaining to the immaterial sphere. Which states are included?

Wholesome, unwholesome, and indeterminate states associated with the taints, whether belonging to the sense sphere, the fine-material sphere, or the immaterial sphere— the aggregate of form, the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of volitional formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—
these states are included. Which states are not included?
The paths, the fruits of the paths, and the unconditioned element—these phenomena are not included [within the realms].
6. The Section on Productive Karma and the Lifespan Limit.
6.1. Productive Karma.
"Devas": there are three kinds of devas—
There are conventional deities, deities by birth, and deities by purification.
Conventional deities are kings, queens, and princes.
The so-called "deities by birth" refers to the deities starting from the Cātumahārājika realm and those above them.
The so-called "pure deities" refers to—
They are called Arahants.
Having given gifts, having undertaken moral discipline, and having performed the Uposatha rites, where do they reappear?
Having given gifts, having undertaken moral discipline, and having performed the Uposatha rites, some are reborn among the wealthy Khattiyas.
Some are reborn into companionship with great brahmin householders;
some are reborn into companionship with great householder householders; some are reborn into companionship with the gods of the Four Great Kings;
some are reborn into companionship with the gods of the Thirty-three; some are reborn into companionship with the Yāma gods.
They are reborn in the company of the gods; some are reborn in the company of the Tusita gods,
some are reborn in the company of the Nimmānarati gods, and some are reborn in the company of the Paranimmitavasavatti gods.
6.2. Life Span.
What is the measure of the life span of human beings?
One hundred years, or somewhat more.
What is the lifespan of the gods of the Four Great Kings?
Fifty human years constitute one day and night for the gods of the Four Great Kings.
Thirty such nights make a month.
By that month, twelve months make a year.
By that year, five hundred divine years is the lifespan of the gods of the Four Great Kings.
How much is that by human calculation?
Ninety-four hundred thousand years.
What is the lifespan of the Tāvatiṃsa devas?
One human century is a single day and night for the Tāvatiṃsa devas.
Thirty nights of that [human] night make a month.
Twelve months of that month make a year.
One thousand divine years of that year is the measure of the lifespan of the Tāvatiṃsa devas.
By human calculation, how much is it?
It is three hundred and sixty million years.
What is the measure of the lifespan of the Yāma devas?
Two hundred human years constitute one day and night for the Yāma devas.
Thirty such nights make a month,
and twelve such months make a year.
By that reckoning, two thousand celestial years is the lifespan of the Yāma devas.
By human calculation, how much is that?
It is fourteen billion and four million years.
What is the lifespan of the Tusita devas?
Four hundred human years constitute a single day and night for the Tusita devas.
Thirty such nights make a month.
Twelve months of that [lunar] reckoning make one year.
Four thousand such divine years is the lifespan of the Tusita devas.
By human calculation, how much is that?
Fifty-seven koṭis of years and six million years.
What is the lifespan of the Nimmānarati devas?
Eight hundred human years constitute a single day and night for the Nimmānarati devas.
Thirty nights of that [human] night make a month.
Twelve months of that month make a year.
Eight thousand divine years of that year is the lifespan of the Nimmānarati devas.
By human calculation, how long is it?
It is two hundred and thirty-four million years.
What is the measure of the lifespan of the Paranimmitavasavatti devas?
Sixteen hundred human years constitute one day and night for the Paranimmitavasavatti devas.
Thirty such nights make a month,
and twelve such months make a year.
By that reckoning, sixteen thousand celestial years is the lifespan of the Paranimmitavasavatti devas.
By human calculation, how much is this?
It is nine hundred and twenty-one million and six hundred thousand years.
These six belong to the sense-sphere,
possessing all sensual pleasures;
they are reckoned as one among them all.
How long is their lifespan?
It is twelve hundred and twenty-eight billion years.
"Fifty hundred thousand years are proclaimed as its lifespan.
Having developed the first jhāna to a limited degree, where are they reborn?
Having developed the first jhāna to a limited degree, they are reborn into the company of the gods of Brahmā’s Retinue.
What is the measure of their lifespan? One-third of an eon.
Having developed the first jhāna to a middling degree, where are they reborn?
Having developed the first jhāna to a middling degree, they are reborn into the company of the Brahmapurohita devas.
What is the measure of their lifespan?
A half-eon.
Having developed the first jhāna to a refined degree, where are they reborn?
Having developed the first jhāna to a refined degree, they are reborn into the company of the Mahābrahmā devas.
What is the measure of their lifespan?
An eon.
Having developed the second jhāna to a limited degree, where are they reborn?
Having developed the second jhāna to a limited degree, they are reborn into the company of the Parittābha devas.
What is the measure of their lifespan?
Two eons (kappa).
Having developed the second jhāna to a middling degree, where are they reborn?
Having developed the second jhāna to a middling degree, they are reborn into the company of the Appamāṇābha devas.
What is the measure of their lifespan?
Four eons.
Having developed the second jhāna in its sublime form, where are they reborn?
Having developed the second jhāna in its sublime form, they are reborn into the company of the Ābhassara devas.
What is the measure of their lifespan?
Eight eons.
Having developed the third jhāna to a limited degree, where are they reborn?
Having developed the third jhāna to a limited degree, they are reborn into the company of the Parittasubha devas.
What is the measure of their lifespan?
It is sixteen eons (kappa).
Having developed the third jhāna to a middling degree, where are they reborn?
Having developed the third jhāna to a middling degree, they are reborn into the company of the Appamāṇasubha devas.
What is the measure of their lifespan?
Thirty-two eons.
Having developed the sublime third jhāna, where are they reborn?
Having developed the sublime third jhāna, they are reborn into the company of the Subhakiṇha devas.
What is their lifespan?
Sixty-four eons.
Having developed the fourth jhāna, there is diversity of object, diversity of attention, diversity of desire, and diversity of aspiration.
There is diversity in resolution, diversity in aspiration, and diversity in wisdom; some are reborn in companionship with the non-percipient beings in the deva realm,
some are reborn in companionship with the Vehapphala devas,
some are reborn in companionship with the Aviha devas, and some are reborn in companionship with the Atappa devas.
Some are reborn in the company of the Sudassāna devas; some are reborn in the company of the Sudassī devas; some are reborn in the company of the Akaniṭṭha devas;

They are reborn in companionship with the gods; some are reborn in companionship with the gods who have attained the base of nothingness, and some are reborn in companionship with the gods who have attained the base of neither-perception-nor-non-perception.
What is the lifespan of the non-percipient beings and the gods of the Great Fruit (Vehapphala)?

Of the seven types of consciousness, how many are mundane and how many are supramundane?
The aggregate of form is mundane.
The four aggregates may be mundane or they may be supramundane.
Ten bases are mundane.
Two bases may be either mundane or supramundane.
Sixteen elements are mundane.
Two elements may be mundane, or they may be supramundane.
Two truths are mundane.
Two truths are supramundane.
Six faculties are mundane.
Three faculties are supramundane.
Nine faculties may be either mundane or supramundane.
The three unwholesome roots are mundane.
The six roots may be either mundane or supramundane.
Edible food is mundane.
Three nutriments may be mundane, or they may be supramundane.
Six types of contact are mundane.
Mind-consciousness-element-contact may be mundane, or it may be supramundane.
Six feelings are mundane.
Feeling born of mind-consciousness-element-contact may be mundane or supramundane.
Six perceptions are mundane.
Perception born of contact with the mind-consciousness element may be mundane or supramundane.
The six types of volition are mundane.
Volition born of contact with the mind-consciousness element may be mundane or supramundane.
Six consciousnesses are mundane.
The mind-consciousness element may be mundane or supramundane.
The two higher knowledges have objects.
Wholesome feeling has been seen;
likewise, resultant [feeling] that is clung-to,
and thought that is mundane and pertaining to the form-world.
The Analysis of the Heart of the Dhamma is finished.
The Book of Analysis is finished.
